AMERICAN ARBITRATION ASSOCIATION
COMMERCIAL ARBITRATION TRIBUNAL

DEMAND FOR ARBITRATION

Claimant: Pelagic Marine Systems, Inc., a Washington corporation
1400 Shipyard Way, Suite 300, Bremerton, Washington 98337
Counsel: Ingrid Halloran, Halloran & Voss LLP, 900 Fourth Avenue, Suite 3800, Seattle, Washington 98164

Respondent: Kanaan Offshore Services LLC, a Louisiana limited liability company
77 Bayou Terrace, Houma, Louisiana 70360
Counsel: unknown at the time of filing

Re: Demand for Arbitration under the Vessel Refit and Services Agreement dated March 9, 2024

1. ARBITRATION AGREEMENT AND JURISDICTION

1.1 Claimant demands arbitration under Section 18.4 of the Vessel Refit and Services Agreement between Claimant and Respondent dated March 9, 2024 (the "Agreement"), which provides that "any dispute arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall be finally resolved by binding arbitration administered by the American Arbitration Association under its Commercial Arbitration Rules, before a panel of three arbitrators, seated in Seattle, Washington."

1.2 The parties' agreement to arbitrate is enforceable under the Federal Arbitration Act, 9 U.S.C. §§ 1–16, and the transactions at issue involve interstate and maritime commerce.

2. THE PARTIES

2.1 Claimant Pelagic Marine Systems, Inc. designs and installs vessel propulsion and control systems.

2.2 Respondent Kanaan Offshore Services LLC owns and operates a fleet of offshore supply vessels, including the M/V Bayou Sentinel.

3. NATURE OF THE DISPUTE

3.1 Under the Agreement, Claimant refitted the propulsion and dynamic-positioning systems of the M/V Bayou Sentinel for a fixed price of $4,275,000, subject to change orders.

3.2 Claimant completed the work and delivered the vessel on February 14, 2026. Respondent accepted delivery, placed the vessel into service, and has operated it continuously since.

3.3 Respondent has paid $2,850,000 of the contract price. Respondent has refused to pay the final milestone payment of $1,425,000, which became due thirty (30) days after delivery, and has refused to pay $612,400 in approved change orders.

3.4 Respondent asserted in correspondence dated April 3, 2026 that the dynamic-positioning system does not meet the specification. Claimant's sea-trial records, countersigned by Respondent's port engineer, show that the system met every acceptance criterion in Exhibit C to the Agreement.

4. CLAIMS FOR RELIEF

4.1 Breach of Contract. Respondent breached the Agreement by failing to pay the final milestone payment and the approved change orders when due. Claimant is entitled to damages of $2,037,400, plus contractual interest at one percent (1%) per month from the respective due dates.

4.2 Breach of the Implied Covenant. Respondent breached the implied covenant of good faith and fair dealing by manufacturing a pretextual specification dispute to avoid payment.

4.3 Unjust Enrichment. In the alternative, Respondent has been unjustly enriched by retaining the benefit of Claimant's work without paying for it.

4.4 Attorneys' Fees. Section 18.7 of the Agreement entitles the prevailing party to its reasonable attorneys' fees and costs, including the fees of the arbitrators and the administrative fees of the American Arbitration Association.

5. RELIEF REQUESTED

Claimant requests an award: (a) of $2,037,400 in damages; (b) of contractual interest at one percent (1%) per month from each due date until paid; (c) of Claimant's reasonable attorneys' fees, costs, and arbitration expenses; and (d) granting such other relief as the panel deems just.

6. ARBITRATOR SELECTION, SEAT, AND HEARING

6.1 Claimant requests a panel of three arbitrators, appointed under the Commercial Arbitration Rules, at least one of whom has experience in marine engineering or shipyard construction contracts.

6.2 The seat of the arbitration is Seattle, Washington, and the hearing locale requested is Seattle, Washington.

6.3 The governing law is the law of the State of Washington, as Section 18.3 of the Agreement provides.

6.4 Claimant estimates that the hearing will require five (5) days.

7. FILING FEE

Claimant submits the filing fee prescribed by the Commercial Arbitration Rules fee schedule for a claim of this amount, and requests that the administrative fees be allocated in the final award.

8. CERTIFICATE OF SERVICE

I certify that on May 6, 2026 I caused a copy of this Demand for Arbitration to be served on Respondent by certified mail, return receipt requested, and by electronic mail, at the addresses stated above, in accordance with Rule R-4 of the Commercial Arbitration Rules.
